We should add "If the resource referred to by volumeAttributesClass does not exist, this PersistentVolumeClaim will be set to a Pending state, as reflected by the modifyVolumeStatus field, until such as a resource exists."
nit: why don't use `opts.EnableVolumeAttributesClass` consistently for all feature gate enablement check?

when an old pvc has this field, it's forbidden for users to update this field when the feature-gate is disable. If an old pvc has this field, the opts.EnableVolumeAttributesClass will be true whatever this feature-gate is enabled or not. 

FYI: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121104/files#diff-c713e8919642d873fdf48fe8fb6d43e5cb2f53fd601066ff53580ea655948f0dR2046
Did we consider having this information as a separate column so that the table remains easily machine readable? (Or is this an already common thing to do?)
It follows the existing pattern, please see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/printers/internalversion/printers.go#L2400

If I understand correctly, the `VolumeAttributesClass` alpha API must also be enabled for this feature to be usable, but that this flag enables the functionality. Can we clarify that here to help prevent confusing when trying this out?
@liggitt @msau42 Should we doing anything more than I suggested above to help cluster admins properly configure a feature that requires both a API be enabled and a feature gate be enabled?

based on [this discussion](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/4298#discussion_r1368102451), I want to make this parameters field become required and add new comment like:

```go
// This field is required and must contain at least one key/value pair.
```

What do you think? @msau42 @sunnylovestiramisu

The problem is that for volume creation, it is not required. So it may not be appropriate to put it in the VAC object.

Or you need to say if it is for a modify volume call, "This field is required and must contain at least one key/value pair."

Right now this API has a couple ways to have "no parameters":

- Empty string for `PersistentVolumeClaimSpec.VolumeAttributesClassName`
- `VolumeAttributesClass` with unset Parameters
- `VolumeAttributesClass` with empty Parameters map

It's not entirely clear if these are all exactly the same, or if there is some subtle difference between them.

If we can simplify the API such that there is only one way to have "no parameters", that would seem best. It would make the API more consistent, easier to understand usages and less prone to subtle and unexpected differences in behavior cause by usages that seem "conceptually same but slightly different in how they are expressed in the API".  Is that possible?

Note that, today, once `PersistentVolumeClaimSpec.VolumeAttributesClassName` is set to a non-empty value, it cannot be set to an empty string, so if we decide to require that Parameters be a non-empty map (at least one entry), we're also making it impossible to set the params to "no parameters" once set to some value. Is that what we want? Since, today ,it would be possible to create a `VolumeAttributesClass` with no parameters and set `PersistentVolumeClaimSpec.VolumeAttributesClassName` to the newly created `VolumeAttributesClass`, we should be careful how we change this so we don't loose the capability to set a PVC to an empty parameter set for use cases where that is sometimes needed.

Agree, the way for someone to specify no parameters is to set their PVC.spec.vacName to "". So VAC.parameters should be required.

I think the awkward scenario though is the backwards compatible scenario for PVC.spec.vacName. We want nil to mean use the default VAC, however we don't want to change existing PVCs which will also have vacName as nil. We *could* have some conditional behavior like "we only set default VAC if PVC is unbound", which will change behavior for new PVCs but not existing ones, but it does mean "no vac" can have 2 ways to express it: 1) nil vacName when bound 2) empty string vacName
updated

I think similar to what we've done with StorageClass, we will want to distinguish between empty and nil values, so that users can indicate they don't want any VAC. Right now nil means that the default will be applied (and that should also be documented here).
Do we allow users to update it with a non-empty value when it's an empty value?
Yes that should be allowed

@msau42 

For static provisioning, if a pvc has a vac and there're 2 pv, one has this vac and another doesn't has vac, which pv will be bound by pvc? In other words, Does vacs take affect on the existing bound logic? BTW, If a user create a pv with a vac specified, but this volume actually doesn't has this attributes defined in the vac. What happened? If the pv doesn't belongs to csi volume when a user create it, what happened? In which case users want to changes the vac of a pv from an empty value to other in the static provisioning case. If we want to allows users to indicate they don't want any VAC on a pv, Is it enough to apply only this rule on the pvc definition and disallow empty value on the pv definition.
These are good questions. @sunnylovestiramisu do you want to think about these corner cases?

Oh, I just realized this is on the PV object. I meant for my original comment to be referring to PVC object.

For PV object, nil is fine to mean does not belong to any VAC. This is inconsistent with PV.Spec.StorageClassName which is a non-pointer field, but that was before we added the guidance that all new fields should be pointers.

PersistentVolumeClaimSpec.VolumeAttributesClassName:
* nil has two meanings: 1. if the PVC is bound, no VAC, similar to empty case. 2. if the PVC is unbound, the user wants to set with the default VAC
* empty means no VAC set on PVC

In PV object we should only have nil and string value, no empty.

For static provisioning, if a pvc has a vac and there're 2 pv, one has this vac and another doesn't has vac, which pv will be bound by pvc?

Answer: vac in the pvc and pv needs to match.


If a user create a pv with a vac specified, but this volume actually doesn't has this attributes defined in the vac. What happened?

Answer: Only admin creates the VAC, so if they made a mistake, we still bind.


In which case users want to changes the vac of a pv from an empty value to other in the static provisioning case.
Answer: we should allow this behavior.

If the pv doesn't belongs to csi volume when a user create it, what happened? 
Answer: This is a csi feature so we should not bind this PV, we can add validation at PV controller that you can only set VAC for a csi volume.

Admin creates the PV object. So we put more trust that they will do the right thing.

Also I think the pv csi validation could also be done in api validation.
Who is responsible for setting the CurrentVolumeAttributesClassName field in the static provisioning, pv controller, csi driver or pvc creator?

> Admin creates the PV object. So we put more trust that they will do the right thing.
> 
> Also I think the pv csi validation could also be done in api validation.

@msau42 It's added in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121104/commits/0c9fae3e297ebec32aab5f86c342c045ba08c39b, please review again.

> Who is responsible for setting the CurrentVolumeAttributesClassName field in the static provisioning, pv controller, csi driver or pvc creator?

PV controller handles static provisioning case, csi-provisioner handles dynamic provisioning case.
Add a note "When unset, there is no VolumeAttributeClass applied to this PersistentVolumeClaim"
If needed at all, "like iops and throughput" might be better put on the API declaration. Here it might be better to state what resources are allowed to do what with this feature?

We refer to this operation as ModifyVolume, ControllerModifyVolume, and VolumeAttributesModify in different places in the api. We should be consistent and pick one name.

cc @gnufied @sunnylovestiramisu for discussion.
ControllerModifyVolume?
